The Trench Funnel primitive synthesizes three core dimensions: environmental (air density), human (injury availability), and market (Kalshi pricing). These form a triadic causal lattice where each node influences others through probabilistic pathways. Air density modifies physical dynamics, which in turn affects player performance and thus market expectations. Injury availability shifts positional probability distributions, altering expected game states. Market sentiment acts as a feedback mechanism, anchoring predictions against empirical consensus. The interplay creates a dualistic structure: one side governed by deterministic biomechanics and the other by stochastic behavioral economics. Failure modes arise when any component is misaligned—e.g., ignoring air effects leads to inaccurate deep-ball projections, or overlooking injuries skews lineup probabilities. The system's robustness depends on maintaining coherence across these layers.
